Proto.About.Intro: As new PCL forks emerge, recreating the UI has become a challenge for developers. PCL.Proto was created to help.
Proto.About.Description: Based on PCL2 by LTCat and PCL2-CE, this project provides a standard prototype for PCL forks. It is built with Vue 3 and can be reused in projects with a WebView frontend.

Proto.Help.Join.Title: What if joining a lobby times out?
Proto.Help.Join.Body: Check the EasyTier settings under multiplayer settings. Both players should have at least one node in common so they can discover each other.
Proto.Help.Start.Title: What if EasyTier fails to start?
Proto.Help.Start.Body: Check whether antivirus software is blocking EasyTier and whether your network can reach the data server. For help, join the user group or report the issue on GitHub.
Proto.Help.Server.Title: Can I use a Minecraft server for multiplayer?
Proto.Help.Server.Body: Yes. Minecraft servers can also be used for multiplayer.
Proto.Help.Identity.Title: Is real-name verification required?
Proto.Help.Identity.Body: It is currently not required. Enter a username in multiplayer settings or sign in with a Natayark account. Refer to announcements and the current service requirements for changes.
Proto.Help.Launchers.Title: Can players using different launchers play together?
Proto.Help.Launchers.Body:
PCL CE and HMCL (Terracotta) support basic interoperability. You can share lobby codes and play with friends using HMCL (Terracotta).

PCL CE is also working with HTML on Scaffolding (a working title), a protocol for multiplayer across launchers, with more features planned.
Proto.Help.Nat.Title: What is a NAT type, and does it affect multiplayer?
Proto.Help.Nat.Body:
Yes, but the effect is usually small when using lobbies. Read on for a brief introduction.

NAT maps multiple private IP addresses to one public IP address. A less restrictive NAT environment makes peer-to-peer connections more likely to succeed and can reduce latency. Most home broadband connections in mainland China use port-restricted cone or symmetric NAT.

You can also read the Tailscale article below (in English) for a deeper explanation.
